note: Adapted from the species-level description in NasuteMandibles1987, originally in English. The original describes only the mandibular dentition of the worker (the sole caste studied in this paper), has no body-length or other measurements, and gives only the left mandible index; the alate mandibles were not observed directly and are only inferred to resemble those of the worker from Mathews (1977: 233-234, fig. 166). OCR problems: occasional double spaces between words and page numbers caught in a line; the dentition terminology is legible.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Left mandible: posterior margin of the apical tooth strongly concave; cutting edge between the first + second marginal teeth and the third marginal tooth undulate; third marginal tooth extremely reduced, visible as a small point in front of the molar tooth; gap between the third marginal tooth and the molar prominence narrow; molar tooth well developed, mostly concealed beneath the molar prominence. Right mandible: posterior margin of the apical tooth strongly concave; second marginal tooth rounded, situated about halfway between the tip of the first marginal tooth and the molar plate; posterior margin of the second marginal tooth concave. Left mandible index in the worker 1.46; Mathews' modified left mandible index in the worker about 1.15. The worker caste is monomorphic.
